card.name: Tautoga
card.profile: The tautoga is considered the most formal and restrained style of Rotuman dance, performed at large festivities and ceremonies (kato'aga) on the island of Rotuma, a Polynesian-outlier dependency of Fiji since 1881 (Wikipedia). Comparable to the Tongan lakalaka and Tuvaluan fatele, it is performed by a dance group (hafa) of 10 to 100+ people arranged in rows, men on one side and women on the other. It is structured as a suite of three dance types - sua, tiap hi'i and tiap forau - accompanied by elders beating a pile of folded mats with sticks. Dancers wear the ha'fali (a sulu-like wrap), tefui garlands and a sweet-smelling flower in the ear (Wikipedia).
card.insight: As the centrepiece of Rotuman kato'aga and a marker of a culture whose language is endangered, the tautoga is treated respectfully as ethnographic ceremony rather than entertainment; it remains central to Rotuman Language Week celebrations across the diaspora (PMN).
